chapter: Harlem, the Cotton Club and Duke Ellington
title: No guitar parts existed; how Fred Guy read
summary: There were no guitar charts for him, so he had to play by ear, while Fred Guy read chord charts on banjo.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Did they have the guitar parts then, did they have the chords written out in notes, or did they have just the letter names?
They didn't have nothing down there for me at all.
Oh, so you had to learn --
I had to do it by ear. If I was going I had to do it by ear, because he didn't have the notes for no guitar, period.
Oh, so even if you could have read there was nothing for you to read.
No.
Because nobody knew how to write for the guitar at that point.
That's right. I don't say Duke didn't know, because he could read period.
But there wasn't no charts.
He could read fly skids, back-to-back.
(Unintelligible)
Yeah. But there wasn't any charts.
But there wasn't no charts for me.
How did Fred Guy play?
Fred Guy didn't have to read -- I mean he reads.
Uh-huh.
Fred Guy read.
But what did he read? Did they have a banjo part?
He read his chart.
Uh-huh. Just with the chords written down?
Yeah. He didn't pick nothing.
Uh-huh. So he had it easy in a way.
Yeah. He had it easier than I did.
But if you were going to have a chart it would probably have lines, single string stuff.
Yeah.
